title: Two Sum

examples.explanation: The numbers at indices 0 and 1 add up to the target 9.
The numbers at indices 1 and 2 add up to the target 6.
The two numbers at indices 0 and 1 add up to the target 6.

title: Product of Array Except Self
description: Return an array where each element is the product of all elements in the array except the element at that position.

examples.explanation: For each position, multiply every number except the number at that position.
Because the array contains zero, the products for every position except the zero position become zero.
Each result contains the product of the other three numbers.

hints: Consider calculating prefix products.
Consider calculating suffix products.
You can achieve O(n) time without using division.
constraints: The array contains at least two integers.

title: 3Sum
description: Find all unique triplets in the array that sum to zero.

examples.explanation: The unique triplets that sum to zero are [-1, -1, 2] and [-1, 0, 1].
There are no three numbers whose sum is zero.
The three zeros form one unique triplet.

hints: Sort the array before searching for triplets.
Use two pointers after fixing the first element.
Skip duplicate values to avoid duplicate triplets.
constraints: Each triplet must contain exactly three numbers.

title: Valid Anagram
description: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s, and false otherwise.

examples.explanation: Both strings contain the same characters with the same frequencies.
The strings contain different characters, so they are not anagrams.
The strings have different lengths and therefore cannot be anagrams.

hints: Anagrams must have the same length.
Count the frequency of each character in both strings.
You can also sort both strings and compare them.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters.
The strings can have different lengths.
Return true only when the character frequencies are identical.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

examples.explanation: The longest substring without repeating characters is "abc", which has length 3.
Every character is the same, so the longest substring contains only one character.
The longest substring without repeating characters is "wke", which has length 3.

hints: Use a sliding window to maintain a substring without duplicate characters.
Keep track of the characters currently inside the window.
Move the left side of the window when a duplicate character is found.
constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, symbols, and spaces.
Return the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

title: Minimum Window Substring
description: Given two strings s and t, return the minimum window substring of s that contains every character in t, including duplicate characters.

examples.explanation: BANC is the smallest substring of s that contains A, B, and C.
The entire string contains the required character.
There are not enough occurrences of a in s to form a valid window.

hints: Use a sliding window with two pointers.
Track the frequency of characters required from t.
Expand the right side until the window is valid, then shrink it from the left.
constraints: s and t consist of English letters.
Return an empty string if no valid window exists.

title: Reverse Linked List
description: Reverse a singly linked list.

examples.explanation: The linked list is reversed.
The two nodes are reversed.
A single-node list remains unchanged.

title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
description: Given the head of a linked list, remove the nth node from the end of the list and return the head of the modified list.

examples.explanation: The second node from the end is 4, so it is removed.
The only node is the first node from the end, so removing it leaves an empty list.
The last node, 2, is removed.

hints: A two-pointer technique can find the target node in one pass.
Move the fast pointer n positions ahead of the slow pointer.
A dummy node can simplify the case where the head itself must be removed.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is between 1 and 100.
1 <= n <= number of nodes in the list.

title: Merge k Sorted Lists
description: Given an array of k linked lists, where each linked list is sorted in ascending order, merge all the linked lists into one sorted linked list.

examples.explanation: The three sorted linked lists are merged into one sorted linked list.
There are no linked lists to merge.
The only linked list is empty, so the merged result is empty.

hints: You can merge the lists pair by pair.
A priority queue can efficiently keep track of the smallest current node.
The heap-based approach can achieve O(N log k) time, where N is the total number of nodes.
constraints: k is the number of linked lists.
The total number of nodes across all linked lists is at most 10000.
Each linked list is sorted in ascending order.

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
description: Find maximum depth of binary tree.

examples.explanation: The maximum depth of the binary tree is 3.
The maximum depth of the binary tree is 2.
A single-node tree has depth 1.

hints: Consider recursively finding the depth of the left and right subtrees.
The depth of an empty tree is 0.
The depth of a non-empty tree is one plus the maximum depth of its subtrees.
constraints: Each node contains an integer value.
Return the maximum number of nodes along a root-to-leaf path.

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return its level order traversal as a list of lists, where each inner list contains the node values at one level of the tree.

examples.explanation: The tree is traversed level by level from left to right.
The tree contains a single node, so the traversal has one level.
An empty tree has no levels.

hints: Use breadth-first search to process the tree level by level.
A queue can store nodes waiting to be processed.
Process all nodes currently in the queue before moving to the next level.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is between 0 and 2000.
Return an empty list when the tree is empty.

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the maximum path sum of any non-empty path in the tree.

examples.explanation: The path 2 → 1 → 3 has the maximum sum of 6.
The path 15 → 20 → 7 has the maximum sum of 42.
The maximum path consists of the root node with value 2.

hints: For each node, calculate the maximum path contribution that can be extended to its parent.
Negative child contributions should not be included in a path.
Track the maximum path that passes through each node separately from the value returned to its parent.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is between 1 and 30000.
Node values are integers between -1000 and 1000.
A path may start and end at any nodes but must contain at least one node.

title: Number of Islands
description: Given an m x n grid of '1's and '0's, return the number of islands in the grid. An island is surrounded by water and is formed by connecting adjacent land cells horizontally or vertically.

examples.explanation: All the connected land cells form one island.
There are three separate groups of connected land cells.
There are no land cells, so there are no islands.

hints: Traverse every cell in the grid.
When you find an unvisited land cell, start a DFS or BFS to visit the entire island.
Count how many times a new island traversal is started.
constraints: Adjacent land cells are connected horizontally or vertically.

title: Course Schedule
description: There are numCourses courses labeled from 0 to numCourses - 1. Given prerequisite pairs, determine whether it is possible to finish all courses.

examples.explanation: Course 0 must be completed before course 1, so both courses can be completed.
The prerequisites form a cycle, so neither course can be completed first.
There are no prerequisites, so all courses can be completed.

hints: Model the courses and prerequisites as a directed graph.
A cycle in the prerequisite graph means the courses cannot all be completed.
You can use DFS cycle detection or Kahn's topological sorting algorithm.
constraints: Each prerequisite pair contains two course numbers.

title: Word Ladder
description: Given two words beginWord and endWord and a dictionary of words, return the number of words in the shortest transformation sequence from beginWord to endWord.

examples.explanation: One shortest transformation is hit → hot → dot → dog → cog.
The end word is not present in the dictionary, so no valid transformation exists.
The transformation a → c changes one character and contains two words.

hints: Treat each word as a node in a graph.
Two words are connected when they differ by exactly one character.

constraints: The word list contains words of the same length.

title: Climbing Stairs
description: You are climbing a staircase. It takes n steps to reach the top. Each time you can climb either 1 or 2 steps. Return the number of distinct ways you can reach the top.

examples.explanation: There are two ways to reach the top: 1 + 1 or 2.
There are three ways: 1 + 1 + 1, 1 + 2, and 2 + 1.

hints: Think about the last step taken to reach the top.
The number of ways to reach step n depends on the ways to reach steps n-1 and n-2.
This problem follows the same recurrence as the Fibonacci sequence.
constraints: You can climb either 1 or 2 steps at a time.
Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top.

title: Coin Change
description: Given an array of coin denominations and an integer amount, return the fewest number of coins needed to make up that amount. If the amount cannot be made up, return -1.

examples.explanation: The minimum number of coins is 3: 5 + 5 + 1.
There is no combination of 2-value coins that produces 3.
No coins are needed to make an amount of zero.

hints: Define a DP state representing the minimum number of coins needed for each amount.
For every amount, try using each available coin.
Build the solution from smaller amounts toward the target amount.
constraints: Each coin denomination may be used an unlimited number of times.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
description: Given two strings text1 and text2, return the length of their longest common subsequence. A subsequence is formed by deleting some characters without changing the order of the remaining characters.

examples.explanation: The longest common subsequence is "ace", which has length 3.
The two strings are identical, so the entire string is their longest common subsequence.
The strings have no characters in common, so their longest common subsequence has length 0.

hints: Compare the characters at the current positions in both strings.
If the characters match, include that character in the subsequence.
If they do not match, consider skipping a character from either string and keep the larger result.
constraints: text1 and text2 consist only of lowercase English characters.
Return the length of the longest common subsequence.

title: Valid Parentheses
description: Given a string containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.

examples.explanation: The opening and closing parentheses match correctly.
Every opening bracket has the correct corresponding closing bracket.

When you encounter a closing bracket, check whether it matches the most recent opening bracket.

Each closing bracket must match the most recently opened bracket.

title: Daily Temperatures
description: Given an array of daily temperatures, return an array where each element represents how many days you have to wait until a warmer temperature. If there is no future day with a warmer temperature, use 0.

examples.explanation: For example, after 73 degrees you wait one day for 74 degrees, while after 75 degrees you wait four days for 76 degrees.
Each temperature has a warmer temperature immediately on the next day except the last one.
Each temperature is followed by a warmer temperature on the next day except the final temperature.

hints: A monotonic decreasing stack can keep track of temperatures that are waiting for a warmer day.
Store indices rather than only temperature values.
When the current temperature is warmer than the temperature at the top of the stack, resolve that previous day.
constraints: Return 0 for days with no warmer future temperature.

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
description: Given an array of integers representing the heights of histogram bars where each bar has width 1, return the area of the largest rectangle that can be formed in the histogram.
